correctness.rationale: For a marked succession, its starting value is uniform over n-1 values and all remaining values are uniformly bijected. Each fixed-point conditional probability is exactly 1/(n-1) on the two endpoint/incident classes or (n-3)/((n-1)(n-2)) otherwise. Multiplication by P(succession)=1/n and subtraction of independent marginals produces the claimed matrix. Row sums give endpoint concentration and total covariance; solving its linear homogeneous system gives the exact odd/even ranks. Variance of U follows from the standard block-enumeration probability P(B_i=B_k=1)=1/[n(n-1)] for distinct indices. A standalone independently implemented enumerator verified all matrix entries through n=8 and rank through n=30.

originality.rationale: The assessed result is the cross-covariance of fixed-point and succession indicators on the SAME uniform permutation and its parity-dependent linear kernel. The closest original 2013 theorem proves only equality in marginal distribution of sets, which leaves their within-permutation coupling unspecified. Later 2024 bijections and joint Eulerian polynomials concern different pairs of statistics, or equidistribution of statistics on different permutations. No precise same-permutation cross-moment matrix or stronger theorem determining it was identified in the inspected primary material; historical priority remains an explicit residual risk.
residual_risks: Historical combinatorial generating-function literature may encode the within-permutation joint Fix/Suc law without naming covariance.

value.rationale: The directly motivating 2013 theorem finds a surprising identity of the MARGINAL distributions of successions and truncated fixed points. Their dependence on the original same permutation is a separate natural mathematical question. The full signed matrix exposes positive local/boundary correlations and negative bulk; its rank has an odd/even dichotomy and a nonconstant exactly uncorrelated alternating succession mode. The endpoints explain precisely (n-1)/n of total covariance, while the overall correlation decays as 2/n². These are structural, complete linear-dependence facts across all orders, not arbitrary finite slices or trivial renamings.
